title: Kintampo culture
description: People on the edge of the forest live in villages, keep livestock and make pottery, the earliest settled farming known in the region.

title: Begho founded
description: A market town grows up where the forest meets the savanna, and traders from the Niger come there to buy Akan gold.

title: Portuguese reach the Gold Coast
description: Portuguese sailors find a coast where gold is traded, which draws Europeans to the region for the next four centuries.

title: Elmina Castle built
description: Diogo de Azambuja builds São Jorge da Mina, the first European trading fort in tropical Africa, to buy gold and later to hold slaves.

title: Dutch capture Elmina
description: The Dutch West India Company takes the castle and makes it the centre of its trade on the coast.

title: Cape Coast Castle begun
description: The Swedish Africa Company builds a timber fort that the English later take and make their headquarters and a main slave-trading post.

title: Christiansborg built
description: Denmark builds a fort at Osu that becomes the centre of its trade on the coast and later the seat of the colonial and Ghanaian governments.

title: Battle of Feyiase
description: Osei Tutu defeats Denkyira, and the Asante union under the Golden Stool becomes the leading power of the forest.

title: Asante army reaches the coast
description: An Asante army defeats the Fante and attacks the British fort at Anomabu, the first fighting between Asante and Britain.

title: Battle of Nsamankow
description: An Asante army destroys a small British force and kills the governor, Sir Charles MacCarthy.

title: Battle of Katamanso
description: The British and their coastal allies defeat an Asante army north of Accra, ending Asante control of the coast.

title: Bond of 1844
description: Fante chiefs sign an agreement giving British officials jurisdiction over serious crimes, later treated as a basis of British rule.

title: Fante Confederacy formed
description: The Fante states unite for their own defence and government, but Britain refuses to recognise the confederation and it dissolves in 1873.

title: Dutch hand Elmina to Britain
description: The Netherlands transfers its last forts on the coast, leaving Britain the only European power there.

title: British burn Kumasi
description: An army under Garnet Wolseley takes and burns the Asante capital, and later that year Britain makes the coast a crown colony.

title: Cocoa planted at Mampong
description: Tetteh Quarshie plants cocoa brought from Fernando Po, the start of the crop that becomes the country's main export.

title: Prempeh I deposed
description: British troops occupy Kumasi without a fight and send the Asantehene into exile, ending Asante independence.

title: Aborigines' Rights Protection Society
description: Chiefs and educated townsmen organise against a bill to put land under the Crown and have it withdrawn, the first effective nationalist campaign.

title: War of the Golden Stool
description: The governor's demand for the Golden Stool sets off a rising led by the queen mother Yaa Asantewaa, after which Britain annexes Asante.

title: Accra riots
description: Police shoot three ex-servicemen marching to the governor's castle, and the riots that follow lead Britain to begin constitutional reform.

title: Convention People's Party founded
description: Kwame Nkrumah launches a mass party before a crowd of some 60,000 with the demand for self-government now.

title: Nkrumah's party wins the first general election
description: The Convention People's Party wins while Nkrumah is in prison, and he is released to lead the government.

title: Independence
description: The Gold Coast becomes independent as Ghana under Kwame Nkrumah, an example followed by colonies across Africa.

title: Republic declared
description: Ghana becomes a republic with Nkrumah as its first president.

title: Akosombo Dam completed
description: A dam on the Volta creates one of the world's largest reservoirs and supplies electricity for an aluminium smelter and the towns.

title: Nkrumah overthrown
description: The army and police seize power while Nkrumah is on his way to Hanoi, the first of several coups.

title: Rawlings's first coup
description: Junior officers free Flight Lieutenant Jerry Rawlings and take power, execute three former heads of state and hand over to an elected government within months.

title: Rawlings takes power again
description: Rawlings overthrows President Hilla Limann and goes on to rule for nineteen years.

title: Constitution of the Fourth Republic approved
description: Voters approve a constitution that restores multi-party politics, under which every government since has been elected.

title: Opposition wins the presidency
description: John Kufuor wins the run-off, and power passes peacefully from one elected party to another for the first time.

title: Oil found offshore
place: Jubilee field, off Cape Three Points
description: A large oil field is discovered in deep water off the western coast, and production begins in 2010.
